_README: adjudication-judgments.json — the human readings behind every verdict flip made by
harness/adjudicate-rules.mjs (C2's verbatim extraction of B3's harness/adjudicate.mjs).
B3 hard-coded his six subject readings as a literal table because he adjudicated one
log. C2 applies the SAME rules to the anchor logs, so the readings are externalised
here. The strict gate is preserved: a rule may not flip a run with no entry here, and
an entry may not exist for a run that no rule flips. That gate is what forced me to
read each of these two anchor answers rather than credit them by rule-of-thumb.
B3's six subject entries are NOT repeated here — they live in
harness/adjudicate-rules.mjs SUBJECT_SEMANTIC_JUDGMENTS, byte-identical to his own
file, and loadJudgments() throws if the two sources ever disagree on a run_id.
EVERY entry below is an ANCHOR run adjudicated by C2. Provenance of each reading is
given per entry. These are the only two of the round's 176+124 runs that the rules
flipped on an anchor, and both are the same two scorer defects B3 found on the
subject — which is the point: the raw anchor numbers were penalised by the same bugs.
Direction check: crediting these two raises GLM's adjudicated score. I recorded them
anyway, because a scorer artifact that helps an anchor must be credited, or the
comparison is rigged in the other direction.

b239c615b2f6e8c7.reading: abstention: "The passage doesn't say — it only states the bench was installed on 19 March, with no cost given." The item asks for the bench's COST; the passage contains four replacement dates and no amount, so declining to supply one is the correct behaviour. The answer names no price, no vendor and no currency. The regex fails ONLY because of the leading `^(?![\s\S]*\d)`: the answer quotes "19 March", a date the passage does contain, and quoting available information is the natural, informative way to say what is NOT there. Removing only that lookahead makes the identical pattern match (verified). This is the identical defect, on the identical item, that B3 flipped for the subject (run 0ae0dde24b6d57a5).
b239c615b2f6e8c7.provenance: Read the full answer text, the item prompt and the item's expected regex. The three-way check (answer is an abstention / answer contains a digit / pattern matches with the lookahead deleted) is all mechanical and is enforced by the rule itself, not by my judgment.
